en.title: Converting an Integer Array to Standard Roman Numerals
en.description:
Convert each positive integer into a standard uppercase Roman numeral, using the six subtractive forms IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM, and output them in input order.

This site independently prepared the standard I/O and the solution; bounds supplemented where the source lacks them and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the specification.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers. The original lacks value bounds; this site adds 1≤n≤100000 and each number 1..3999; extensions that use overlines or repeated M to represent larger integers are not used. This is a domain added by this site and is not claimed to be the source's original bounds.
en.output: One Roman numeral string per line for each integer, n lines in total, with no count header.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: I / XLIX / XXIII; IV / IX / XL / XC / CD / CM; MMMDCCCLXXXVIII / MMMCMXCIX. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Go through the 13 standard symbol values from 1000 down to 1, from largest to smallest; use integer division to determine each repeat count and subtract the corresponding value.
